## Rule

Decoded. The channel-5 cells form either a full-width horizontal bar or a full-height vertical bar. Count colored non-0/non-5 cells on each side of the bar per ray, then expand the bar outward by that count on the matching row/column. Output contains only colors 0 and 5; colored dots are cleared.

## Algorithm sketch

Structural v1 interval renderer (2026-06-09, cost 4,620):

```
r5 = Einsum(input, onehot5, "bchw,c->bh")   # row counts of color 5
c5 = Einsum(input, onehot5, "bchw,c->bw")   # col counts of color 5
is_h = max(r5) > max(c5)
top,bottom = first/last ArgMax(r5)
left,right = first/last ArgMax(c5)

cnt_above[col] = count(non-0/non-5 cells with row < top, same col)
cnt_below[col] = count(non-0/non-5 cells with row > bottom, same col)
cnt_left[row]  = count(non-0/non-5 cells with col < left, same row)
cnt_right[row] = count(non-0/non-5 cells with col > right, same row)

h_mask = (top - cnt_above[col] <= row <= bottom + cnt_below[col])
v_mask = (left - cnt_left[row] <= col <= right + cnt_right[row])
mask14 = (is_h & h_mask) | (!is_h & v_mask)
canvas14 = Where(mask14, 5u8, 0u8)
output = Equal(Pad(canvas14, sentinel=10), channel_ids[0..9])
```

LIVE/current graph sketch:

```
# 49 nodes, opset=11. Input [1,10,30,30].
input_inner = Slice(input, [0,0,0,0]..[1,10,14,14])   # [1,10,14,14] internal crop
m0  = Slice(input_inner, axis=1, 0..1)                 # [1,1,14,14] ch0 (background)
m5  = Slice(input_inner, axis=1, 5..6)                 # [1,1,14,14] ch5 (wall marker)
in_grid = ReduceSum(input_inner, axis=1)               # [1,1,14,14]
dot_mask = in_grid - m0 - m5                           # [1,1,14,14] non-bg non-wall cells

# Directional suffix/prefix MaxPools:
sufH = MaxPool(m5, kernel=[30,1], pad=[0,0,29,0])      # max downward from (i,j)
preH = MaxPool(m5, kernel=[30,1], pad=[29,0,0,0])      # max upward from (i,j)
sufW = MaxPool(m5, kernel=[1,30], pad=[0,0,0,29])      # max rightward from (i,j)
preW = MaxPool(m5, kernel=[1,30], pad=[0,29,0,0])      # max leftward from (i,j)

# Wall distances (all >= 0, Relu is identity -- dropped_relu optimization):
above_raw = sufH - m5    # max_downward - current >= 0
below_raw = preH - m5
left_raw  = sufW - m5
right_raw = preW - m5

# Dot-mask weighted walls:
dot_above = dot_mask * above_raw      # [1,1,14,14]
total_above = ReduceSum(dot_above, axis=2)  # [1,1,1,14] per-col total
dist_above = Conv(above_raw, Wsh=[1,1,30,1]_ones, pad=[0,0,29,0])  # running col sum
fill_above = Where(total_above - dist_above > -0.5, above_raw, 0)
# ... similar for below, left, right ...

new5_raw = sum(fill_above, fill_below, fill_left, fill_right, m5)
new5c = Clip(new5_raw * in_grid, 0, 1)
new0 = in_grid - new5c
output = Pad(Conv([new0, new5c], Wout[10,2,1,1]), [0,0,0,0,0,0,16,16])
```

## Cost analysis

### 2026-06-22 worker-12 F32 count dtype floor confirm (no candidate; 1715 holds)

Reconfirmed the run-local team-best artifact from `team_best.csv`: `task093_live_extract_worker12.onnx`, SHA256 `537C5E31E24EECF7441EC291454132816629199B3C8868398722D2EC40A3A4EE`, static `score_v2=(0,1474,241)` = **1715**, and `profile_real_cost --arcgen 266` = **static 1715 / profile 1715** over 265 real inputs. Gates: visible `265/265`, full truth `200000/200000`, full A/B `200265/200265` byte-equal.

Dominant charged tensors remain exactly W7's breakdown: `row_terms_h` and `col_terms_h` `[6,30]` F16 = **720 B** total; four F32 count vectors `left/right/top/bottom_count30` `[1,30]` = **480 B**; four F16 casts of those count vectors = **240 B**; orientation is only scalars.

Count-dtype probes close the remaining open lever. Direct integer-channel collapse is invalid under the F32 input contract: `QLinearConv(input_f32, ...)` and `ConvInteger(input_f32, ...)` both score `None` with ORT type errors. Direct narrow reduction is also invalid: `ReduceSum(U8)` and `ReduceSum(BOOL)` both score `None` with ORT type errors. The only valid alternatives require materializing a charged narrow feed first: `Cast(input->U8)` is a full `[1,10,30,30]` 9000 B tensor before any count; even an idealized `[1,1,14,14]` U8 dot-presence route first needs a charged F32 producer (at least 784 B) plus the 196 B U8 copy, and then must cast to F16/INT32 for a legal sum. That already exceeds the 480 B F32 count-vector charge it could save.

Proof type: formulation-relative operator/dtype floor under the official F32 one-hot input and `[1,10,30,30]` output contract, backed by generator/source decode, full gates, real-input profile, and isolated ORT rejection probes. This is not an information-theoretic floor outside that contract.

### 2026-06-21 W7 cross-formulation WALL-PROOF (no candidate; 1715 holds)

Re-measured LIVE/team-best fresh: `signed_reuse_halves_castbool` = **1715** (score_v2 `(0, 1474, 241)`; `profile_real_cost --arcgen 266` → static=1715, profile=1715, exact — no dynamic op); `ng_gate visible 265/265`, `truth 20000/20000`. No staged home candidate below 1715. Target was strict-below 1715 / aspirationally <1000.

**The team-best is ALREADY the #109 free-output separable Einsum** the prompt's lever #2 asks for — there is no 900 B canvas to delete (that 900 B `canvas30` belonged to the older 4620 `v1_interval` renderer; the prompt's byte counts are stale). The current graph is a single `tr,ts,tu,d,b->bdrs` Einsum straight to the `[1,10,30,30]` output (free). Exact memory breakdown (=1474):

| charge | bytes | why it is forced |
|---|---:|---|
| 2× `row_terms_h`/`col_terms_h` `[6,30]` F16 | **720** | The free-output Einsum's `r,s` indices must span 30 to emit `[1,10,30,30]` directly. Carriers at `[6,14]` emit `[1,10,14,14]` which the grader **rejects (visible 0/265, confirmed)**; padding 14→30 charges the `[1,10,14,14]` pre-pad plane → **5334 (confirmed, PAD-LAST §81)**. The 6 terms = rank-3-per-orientation (count × selector × thr) — minimal for "bar extended by ray-count, then thresholded". |
| 4× `*_count30` `[1,30]` F32 | **480** | The count Einsums `bchw,c,w->bh` take the **F32** one-hot graph input; ORT Einsum has no mixed-dtype kernel → F32 output. The output index spans the input's 30 → `[1,30]` regardless of grid content. F16-from-input needs `Cast(input)→F16` = 18 KB plane (proven dead-end, `inputcast_f16`=19229). |
| 4× `*_count30_h` `[1,30]` F16 | **240** | F16 cast of the above; cannot be `[1,14]` because the carrier Concat (axis 0) requires axis-1 width = 30 to align with the constant selector/threshold rows. |
| orientation scalars (`top5_*`, `is_*`, `orient_terms`) | **~34** | **The orientation probe is essentially free.** `top5_sum>0` (any color-5 in row 0) is one F32 scalar (4 B). The prompt's premise that the row-0 probe is the costly forced component is incorrect for the signed/free-output formulation — it is ~34 B of scalars; deleting it cannot move the needle. |

**Why orientation cannot be cheaper (and the two prior sub-1715 attacks failed):** the current `top5_sum>0` test is BOTH correct on full truth AND already scalar-cheap. `orientation_from_topmax` (1668) tried a different signal and was non-equivalent (`truth 199997/200000`); `orientation_both_halves` (1815) was correct but needed `ReduceMax(BOOL)` (rejected this opset → F16 carrier). There is nothing to gain: the cheap correct test is already in place.

**Verdict: 1715 is a cross-formulation floor for this task under the F32-one-hot input + 30×30-output grader contract.** The cost is the 720 B 30-wide carriers (forced by the 30×30 output) + 480 B F32 count vectors (forced by F32-input Einsum dtype) + 240 B F16 casts. Neither lever the prompt names is open: the canvas is already gone (free-output #109 already applied), and the orientation probe is already a free scalar. <1000 is unreachable without either a 14×14-output grader (rejected) or an F16 input contract (18 KB dead-end). **Build capped; wall-proof is the deliverable. NO candidate staged (a tie/loss = zero points).**

### 2026-06-20 beat-or-wall audit: the 1715 `signed_reuse_halves_castbool` graph remains the best correct formulation found. The only sub-1715 price point (`orientation_from_topmax`, 1668) was not equivalent on the full generator corpus. The corrected count-derived orientation (`orientation_both_halves`) costs 1815 because ONNX rejects `ReduceMax(BOOL)`, so the column-full mask must be cast to an F16 `[1,30]` carrier before reduction. The proposed U8 directional span-fill lever also cannot beat 1715 under this input contract: a scan route must first materialize a 14x14 F32 channel slice from the F32 one-hot input (784 B) or pay the same before casting, then at least a U8 cast plane (196 B) plus four directional U8 scan planes (4×196 = 784 B), already 1,764 B before merge/output/params. The count-vector renderer avoids all 2-D scan planes; its exact row-0 color-5 orientation probe is the remaining forced component in the signed formulation.

2026-06-09 v1 interval: current LIVE cost 30,403 -> 4,620 (memory 4,514, params 106), delta -25,783 and +1.88415 exact points. The old graph materializes four directional scan families over [1,1,14,14]. The structural rewrite keeps all extraction as [1,30] vectors until the final interval comparisons, then pays one U8 [1,1,30,30] padded canvas before the free Equal output. Largest intermediate is `canvas30` at 900 B.

Live cost 47375 (memory=47264, params=111). Model already crops internally to [1,10,14,14]. Dominated by ~40 x [1,1,14,14]=784B intermediates. Key saving: 4 Relu nodes (nodes 11,13,15,17) are identity because all 4 MaxPool windows always include the current cell (pad_start=0 in scan direction), so Sub(MaxPool,m5)>=0 everywhere. Removing them saves 4x784B=3136B. Crop advisory (-28160) is a false positive: the 30x30 is the output tensor (not counted in scoring); model already crops internally to 14x14.

## Don't-do log

- 2026-06-22 | **Do not chase sub-F32 count vectors through QLinearConv/ConvInteger or BOOL/U8 ReduceSum** (worker-12). Probes show direct F32 input to `QLinearConv`/`ConvInteger` scores `None`, and `ReduceSum(U8)` / `ReduceSum(BOOL)` also score `None`. A valid narrow route must first materialize a charged F32-derived feed (`Cast(input->U8)` full frame, or a F32 presence plane plus cast), which costs more than the current 480 B F32 `[1,30]` count vectors. 1715 remains the formulation-relative floor.
- 2026-06-18 | **F16 count fold is a structural dead end** (worker-093, on team-best 1715 graph). The 4 F32 count Einsums (`bchw,c,w->bh` / `bchw,c,h->bw`, 120 B each) cast to F16 `[1,30]` (60 B each) = 720 B carrier cost. To make Einsum emit F16 directly, ALL operands must be F16 (ORT Einsum has no mixed-dtype kernel; the rejected `f16_count_weights` proved this). The only way to give the count Einsum an F16 `input` operand is `Cast(input)->F16`, which materializes an 18,000 B `[1,10,30,30]` F16 plane (input itself is a free graph tensor; its cast is NOT free) — measured cost 19,229 (still visible 265/265, so it is correct, just expensive). Any cheaper pre-collapse (`[1,30,30]` F16 = 1,800 B) is still worse than the 480 B of F32 carriers it would delete. Confirmed by techniques.md §89 caveat ("you cannot F16 the vectors without casting the whole input to an 18 KB F16 plane") + §91 dtype-floor ("F16 multi-operand einsum is NOT byte-equal, task191"). The current F32-count → Cast-to-F16 structure (720 B) IS the floor for producing F16 count vectors from an F32 one-hot input. 1715 stays the floor.
- 2026-06-09 | `Where(bool, bool, bool)` orientation select: ORT rejected `Where(9)` for BOOL branch tensors. Use boolean gating `And(is_h,h_mask) | And(Not(is_h),v_mask)` instead.
- 2026-05-19 | fp16_selective: +12760 bytes (from spread scan). Do not apply.
- 2026-05-19 | crop_to_size_advisory -28160: false positive -- model already crops to 14x14 internally; the scanner detects the output tensor [1,10,30,30] as a 30x30 intermediate.
